title: Shimla Manali Itinerary: 6 to 8 Days in Himachal
seoTitle: Shimla Manali Itinerary: 6 to 8 Days in Himachal | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: A day-by-day Shimla Manali itinerary for six to eight days: Shimla, Kufri, the drive to Manali, Solang, the Atal Tunnel and Naggar, with variations.
description: A practical six to eight day Shimla and Manali itinerary: the Kalka-Shimla toy train, Shimla's Ridge and Kufri, the long drive to Manali through the Kullu valley, Old Manali, Solang valley and the Atal Tunnel to Sissu, Naggar and Kasol, with variations for winter snow, adding Dharamshala, and returning by overnight bus or flight.
dek: Shimla and Manali are India's classic hill-station pairing. Here is a realistic route that leaves time to enjoy both.

hero.alt: The Beas valley near Palchan, above Manali

intro: Shimla and Manali are about 250 km apart, a full day's drive through Mandi and the Kullu valley. Put together, they make one of India's most popular hill holidays: a colonial town on a ridge, then a river valley under snow peaks.
This route assumes you start from Delhi or Chandigarh. It works from March to June and October to February; avoid the peak monsoon weeks, when landslides often disrupt the Kullu valley road.
quickAnswer: A six to eight day Shimla Manali itinerary: travel to Kalka and take the toy train or drive to Shimla (day 1), explore Shimla and Kufri (day 2), drive to Manali via Mandi and Kullu (day 3), see Old Manali, Hadimba and Vashisht (day 4), Solang and the Atal Tunnel to Sissu (day 5), Naggar or Kasol (day 6), then return by overnight bus or via Bhuntar or Chandigarh (days 7 to 8).
takeaways: Allow a full day for the Shimla to Manali drive, about 250 km.
The Kalka-Shimla toy train is slow but scenic; book on IRCTC.
Solang and Sissu (via the Atal Tunnel) are the main snow spots near Manali in winter.
Rohtang Pass needs an online permit and opens only in summer.
Add Dharamshala or Kasol for a longer trip.

rows: Kalka to Shimla by toy train or road; evening on the Ridge
Jakhoo temple, Christ Church, Mall Road; Kufri or Mashobra
Drive via Mandi and Kullu (about 8 to 9 hours)
Old Manali, Hadimba temple, Vashisht hot springs
Solang valley; Atal Tunnel to Sissu in Lahaul
Naggar castle and Roerich estate, or a day in Kasol
Overnight bus to Delhi, or fly from Bhuntar or Chandigarh

items.name: Shimla
body: The toy train from Kalka takes about five to six hours; the road is faster. Spend a day on the Ridge and Mall Road, climb to Jakhoo, and take a half-day trip to Kufri or Mashobra.

image.alt: The Ridge and Mall Road, Shimla
image.caption: Shimla's Ridge

sections.heading: Day 3: Shimla to Manali
paras: The drive follows the Sutlej and then the Beas through Mandi and Kullu. Start early; with stops it takes most of the day. Kullu has river rafting in season, and the Pandoh dam and the Aut tunnel are on the way.

items.name: Kullu
body: The valley town on the way.

items.name: Manali
body: Old Manali's cafés, the Hadimba temple in its cedar grove, Vashisht's hot springs, Solang valley for snow or paragliding, and the Atal Tunnel to Sissu. Naggar's castle and the Roerich estate, or a day in Kasol in the Parvati valley, make a quieter last day.

sections.heading: Variations
list: Winter (December to February): expect snow around Solang and Sissu; roads beyond may close after heavy snowfall. Keep a buffer day.
Summer (May to June): Rohtang Pass can be added with an online permit (closed on Tuesdays).
Add Dharamshala: from Manali, drive to McLeod Ganj (about seven to eight hours) for two nights, then return to Delhi.
Shorter trip: five days, with one day less in each town.

sections.heading: Getting there and back
list: Delhi to Kalka by the Kalka Shatabdi, then toy train or road to Shimla.
Overnight Volvo buses run between Delhi and both Shimla and Manali.
Bhuntar airport (for Manali) and Chandigarh airport have flights, though Bhuntar's are limited and weather-dependent.
A car and driver for the whole trip is the most flexible option.

sections.heading: Where to stay
paras: In Shimla, stay near the Ridge and Mall Road for walkability, or in Mashobra for quiet. In Manali, Old Manali and Vashisht suit younger travellers with cafés close by, while the Naggar and Hadimba sides are calmer for families and couples. Confirm heating in winter and parking if you are driving.

safety: Drive times are approximate and depend on traffic, weather, landslides and road works; allow extra time and avoid driving after dark.
Permits, e-passes, ropeways and pass openings change; check official portals before you travel.
In winter, use drivers experienced in snow, and carry warm layers in the car.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Shimla and Manali?
faqs.a: Six to eight days is comfortable; five is possible but rushed.

faqs.q: How far is Manali from Shimla?
faqs.a: About 250 km, a full day's drive via Mandi and Kullu.

faqs.q: Can I see snow on a Shimla Manali trip?
faqs.a: In winter, Solang, Sissu and Kufri are the likeliest places; snow is never guaranteed.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for Rohtang?
faqs.a: Yes, an online permit, and the pass opens only in summer; the Atal Tunnel needs no permit.

faqs.q: Should I take the toy train to Shimla?
faqs.a: It is a lovely experience but slow; book early, or take it one way only.
